concepts.label: Analytics Workbench (Couchbase Server)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the Couchbase Web Console UI for developing and running Analytics queries and managing links/collections. NEAR-MISS CHECKED against the extraction-layer capella:analytics-workbench (Capella's own Analytics Workbench, cloud/clusters/analytics-service/analytics-workbench.json) - almost certainly the same underlying feature by description, but no page in either tree states the two are the same UI, and the round brief explicitly warns against forcing a Capella/server page-to-page correspondence here, so kept as a separate mint per the no-silent-merge rule. Flagged for reconciliation.

concepts.label: Analytics collection
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the object this page's UI actually manages ('The Analytics Workbench enables you to create, edit, and drop collections'). NEAR-MISS CHECKED against two other unpromoted mints for what may be the same referent: analytics:shadow-collection ('shadow collection / shadow copy (Analytics)', minted from server/8.0/learn/services-and-indexes/services/analytics-service.json, reluctantly, noting capella:analytics-dataset as a likely duplicate already) and capella:analytics-dataset ('a shadow copy of operational data that the Analytics Service creates and keeps in sync in real time', minted from cloud/clusters/analytics-service/analytics-service.json). This page's own text uses the verb 'shadow' identically ('so that collections on the link can shadow data from their data sources'), which is suggestive, but no page anywhere states outright that 'dataset', 'shadow collection' and 'Analytics collection' are three names for one object, so all three ids are kept apart per the standing no-silent-merge rule. See cross_component_finding.

concepts.label: Analytics scope
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the container level above an Analytics collection/link; this page states the Default scope specifically cannot be deleted.

concepts.label: Local link (Analytics)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the always-present link every Analytics scope has for shadowing Data service collections.

concepts.label: Remote link (Analytics)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a link to a remote Couchbase cluster, fully detailed in manage-links.md (this batch).

concepts.label: External link (Analytics)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a link to an external data source (Amazon S3, Azure Blob, Google Cloud Storage). NEAR-MISS CHECKED against capella:analytics-external-link ('a link to an external data source ... that lives within an Analytics scope', cloud/clusters/analytics-service/analytics-links.json) - the two definitions are close to word-for-word identical, but per this round's framing Capella's pages are UI-driven and not to be forced into correspondence with server/'s own pages without a source stating the equivalence, so kept separate. Strong reconciliation candidate.

concepts.label: Keyspace
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - already promoted, used here for the Data service bucket.scope.collection that a mapped or local-link Analytics collection sources its data from.

concepts.label: CREATE ANALYTICS COLLECTION
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the SQL++ for Analytics DDL statement equivalent of creating a collection on a local or remote link via the Workbench. Per the round brief's guidance on DDL-vs-management framing: this page also states a WHERE-clause requirement on the statement itself ('You must not include the WHERE keyword, and the expression must be deterministic') - that constraint belongs to this DDL concept (or to 5_ddl.md's own fuller definition of it), not to the management task, and is recorded on this id rather than modeled as a separate relation here.

concepts.label: CREATE EXTERNAL ANALYTICS COLLECTION
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - sibling DDL statement of analytics:create-analytics-collection, for a collection sourced from an external link rather than a local or remote one.

concepts.label: ALTER COLLECTION
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the DDL statement equivalent of the Workbench's 'Map From Data Service' action; the fact that this SQL++ statement, not just the UI action, performs the mapping is stated directly on this management page rather than on a DDL reference page in this batch.

concepts.label: DROP ANALYTICS COLLECTION
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - DDL equivalent of the Workbench's delete-collection action.

notable_absence.finding: No RBAC gate of any kind is stated anywhere on this page - none of the Workbench actions (map, create, connect, disconnect, delete a collection or scope) name a required role or privilege, unlike Capella's analytics-links.md (this round's background reading), which explicitly gates the Analytics Workbench on Project Owner or Data Writer. Also absent: a stated precondition for deleting a scope ('as long as the scope contains no remote links or external links, and contains no collections on the Local link') is given only as a UI-level caveat, with no error code or DDL-level statement of the same rule cross-referenced from this page.

cross_component_finding: This page is the third independent mint, in three different pages across two products, of what looks like one underlying construct: capella:analytics-dataset ('a shadow copy of operational data ... kept in sync in real time'), analytics:shadow-collection ('shadow collection / shadow copy (Analytics)', minted reluctantly from a Server services-and-indexes page noting the Capella duplicate), and this page's own analytics:analytics-collection ('so that collections on the link can shadow data from their data sources'). All three definitions independently use the word 'shadow' for what appears to be the same mechanism, and none of the three pages states that the others' term is the same thing - a namespace-fork-adjacent situation structurally identical to the registry's own eventing:timer-callback / eventing:timer-callback-handler writeup, flagged there as 'not catchable by an existing instrument.' Recommended for explicit reconciliation attention rather than resolved here.
